lines.text: Zero to one hundred. Grandma's glow up for her class reunion. Tonight at seven.
I'm already at forty. I put on earrings.
Zero percent.
That's the meter, Grandma. It tells us how glowed up you are.
A phone is going to grade me? I raised four boys. Nothing grades me.
I grade everyone. Silently. From the dresser.
That's Biscotti. Retired show cat. He's helping.
Third place, nineteen ninety eight, Ohio. Best Attitude.
Step one. Skincare. What do you wash your face with?
Dish soap. Same bottle since nineteen eighty.
That cannot be the same bottle.
I refill it with hope.
Okay. This is a serum. Three drops.
It says forty dollars. Per drop? I'll drink it.
Ten percent.
I feel moisturized against my will.
She is glistening. Like a rotisserie chicken. That is a compliment.
Step two. Hair. Grandma, when did you last take down the bun?
The moon landing. I was excited, it came loose.
Allow me. I will lick it into shape.
Nobody is licking Grandma.
Okay. Unpinning. Three, two, one.
Release the bun.
Ma'am, that is a lot of hair. Where was it living?
Up there. Rent free. Since nineteen sixty nine.
Twenty seven percent.
Twenty seven? Why are you so slow?
I am doing my best. I am plugged in behind the dresser. It is dusty back here.
Step three. The outfit. What were you going to wear?
My prom dress. It still fits.
Grandma, that's from nineteen seventy one.
I sewed elastic in it in nineteen seventy one. I plan ahead.
It is giving curtains.
It was curtains. Your great grandmother's living room. She never forgave me.
Fifty percent.
Who are we glowing up for, anyway?
Harold Pemberton. At prom he said I danced like a shopping cart.
One wheel that goes its own way. He was right, and I have never let it go.
Last step. Lashes.
Spider. Spider on her face. I will handle this.
Biscotti, those are eyelashes! They cost more than you!
Seventy percent. Charging.
Wait. Charging?
The percent is my battery. You plugged me in when you pressed record.
So the glow up meter was never a meter?
I am a phone. I do not rate grandmas. I would lose.
So what was I at? At the start?
Ma'am. You were at a hundred. I just did not want to say it before the transition.
I knew it. Earrings.
Then why did you let me do all this?
Because you spent a whole Saturday with your grandma. That's my glow up.
I am not crying. I have something in my eye. It is the eyelash.
Incoming call. Harold Pemberton.
Harold? Yes. I still dance like a shopping cart. Wheels and all. See you at seven.
One hundred percent.
Glow up complete! Grandma, you look amazing.
Now sit down, sweetie. Your turn. Zero percent.
Third place. Again.
